new_value: Root cause + fix landed (75b86d62cd). ROOT CAUSE (proven by two-sided instrumentation): lichen_link_load_key rolls a fresh RANDOM epoch per call and resets tx_seq=0; with CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_REPLAY_PERSIST off, the l2 layer never pinned the boot epoch, so the same-key re-provision after ctx teardown moved the epoch backward (full_ping frames epoch=177, udp window epoch=142) and reset the seq — replay-window holders correctly returned EALREADY. l2_input fires exactly once per frame (double-processing hypotheses disproven). FIX: (1) lichen_l2_key.c boot-epoch latch (RAM, guarded to non-REPLAY_PERSIST builds): first load adopts, later loads pinned UP only (never down — post-seq-wrap advanced epochs are latched, never regressed); (2) link_ctx.c RAM nonce-stream checkpoint: cleanup snapshots (pk, epoch, tx_seq, nonce_exhausted) before the wipe; load_key with a matching pk resumes the exact stream position (fresh keypair starts at seq 0 — new replay identity). REVIEW: 3 passes + 1 verification on kimi-k3 — pass 3 caught unused latch statics under REPLAY_PERSIST (guarded) and the missing nonce_exhausted in the checkpoint (restored); pass 2 caught the pin-vs-seq-wrap regression (pin made raise-only; checkpoint carries the epoch); verification PASS. Documented ceiling: single-slot checkpoint loses a prior key's stream on A->B->A rotation within one boot (strictly better than pre-fix; multi-slot = follow-up if ever needed). VALIDATED: ping_l2 native_sim on heft 7/7 PROJECT EXECUTION SUCCESSFUL.
